sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: team-level queries (manager views their direct reports); employment_status: filtering active/inactive/terminated employees

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filtering policies by leave type (annual, sick, emergency); is_active: filtering active policies for assignment and balance calculation

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of leave requests by employee; status: filtering by status (SUBMITTED for manager approval queues); approved_by: manager queries for requests they approved; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; leave_policy_id: filtering by leave type

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: lookups of all balances for an employee; employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year: unique composite lookup for a specific balance row (one balance per employee per policy per fiscal year); leave_policy_id: aggregate queries across employees for a policy; fiscal_year: filtering balances by fiscal year

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: lookups of audit trail for a specific entity; performed_by: audit queries by actor; action: filtering by action type (APPROVE, REJECT, CREATE); performed_at: time-range audit queries

data_notes: Tables defined: employees, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, audit_logs. The employees and leave_policies tables are referenced by leave_requests and leave_balances via FK. The audit_logs table supports GP-002 (all state-changing operations write an audit record). The leave_balances table stores one row per employee per policy per fiscal year; used_days and remaining_days are updated atomically within transactions. The leave_requests.status field uses the LeaveStatus enum values: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted from start_date to end_date — calendar days (inclusive of both ends, e.g. Mon–Fri = 5 days) or business/working days only? This is BINDING across all balance-deduction and overlap-detection call sites.
open_questions.impact: Affects used_days increment/decrement in leave_balances, overlap detection in leave_requests, and the remaining_days computation. Every call site that computes day counts must use the same rule.
candidate_options: Business days only (exclude weekends + holidays from a holiday calendar)

transaction_contract: Repository methods that participate in multi-step writes accept an optional PoolClient parameter (defaulting to the shared pool when omitted). The calling service owns the unit of work: it acquires a client from the pool, executes BEGIN, passes the client to each repository call, and then executes COMMIT or ROLLBACK. This contract applies to: (1) leave request submission — create leave_request + write audit_log; (2) leave request approval/rejection — update leave_request status + increment/decrement leave_balance used_days/remaining_days + write audit_log; (3) leave request cancellation — update leave_request status + decrement leave_balance used_days + write audit_log.
